comment: The parity inventory of 3D-Bausteine 2.0: one record per element and behaviour of
3D-Baukasten 1.3 that the parity plan numbers P-nnn in its sections 1 to 9, plus P-200a, the
record of the window F6 in the EXE, and P-203b, the tool tip of its combo CB3. Notebook 80
reads it as INVENTORY of tests/harness.py and walks it in both looks, and its section 19
writes Documentation/parity.md from it. The fields say what each key of a record means.

fields.id: The number of the parity plan, P-nnn with a letter where the plan has one.
fields.name: What the element or the behaviour is, in English with the German names of 1.3.
fields.selector: A CSS selector that matches the element of the page exactly once, or null for a behaviour without one element.
fields.container: The selector of the window or of the record the element lies in, or null for a window, a dialog or the splash itself and for an entry of a drop-down list, which may reach past its window as a list of Windows does.
fields.tab: The data-tab of the register F4 whose page must be in front first, or null.
fields.order: The index of the element among the elements that group selects, in reading order: top to bottom by rows, where elements whose vertical extents overlap form one row, and left to right inside a row. Null where no order applies.
fields.group: The selector of the elements that order counts, or null.
fields.text: The caption, the legend, the tool tip or the label the element shows, the text of 1.3 wherever 2.0 keeps it. It matches when it equals, with blanks collapsed, the textContent of the element, of its legend or of its first span, or its data-tip, title, aria-label or value. An object with the keys modern and classic gives a text per look, and a look it leaves out has no text to check. For a message it is the text of the message.
fields.looks: The looks in which the element exists at its place, modern, classic or both.
fields.kind: element (a control at a place), menu-entry (an entry of a menu or of a drop-down list, shown once trigger opens it), tooltip (the tool tip of the element is text), state (effect holds, after trigger where one is given), message (a message box or a status text), key (a key that trigger presses, and effect holds after it), behaviour (a behaviour that the section in checkedIn proves) or absent (an element of 1.3 that 2.0 does not build on purpose).
fields.twips: The place of 1.3 as left, top, width and height in twips, 15 to the pixel, relative to the client of the container: the .win-client of a window and the box of any other container. Where a frame of 1.3 is no record, its place is added. Section 17 of notebook 80 compares left and top with the classic look at 1024 by 768 within 2 px.
fields.clipped: The virtual screens of the classic look at which the window cuts the element off or hides it, as Form_Set of 1.3 sizes the window, or null. At those screens the walk does not ask the element to lie inside its container.
fields.trigger: One step before the check, or null: menu:<data-menu> opens a menu of the menu bar, list:<selector> clicks to open a drop-down list, entry:<text> types the text into CB1 as Browser.entry does, act:<entry> runs bausteine.act, click:<selector> clicks, key:<name> presses a key as Browser.key does.
fields.effect: A JavaScript expression of the page that answers true when the record holds, or null.
fields.note: What else the record says, with the IDs of Documentation/quirks.md where a decision stands there.
fields.checkedIn: The notebook sections that prove the record, such as 70 §15. Sections 14 and 15 of notebook 80 count such a record and leave it to them.
